tasks.notes: This TaskInstance represents an ATUS diary coding category at macro-activity granularity, not a single manipulation, a fixed procedure, or an event count. The 2024 ATUS lexicon includes cooking, preparing food, making coffee/tea, mixing drinks, and getting a drink/pouring water in a glass among examples for the category. The existing YCB mug is only the curator-selected Atlas ObjectInstance anchor needed for the two-edge hierarchy traversal; neither the BLS category nor its statistics assert that an activity involved this mug or any specific object. The scene_home_kitchen link is a representative Atlas context, not a claim that every sampled activity occurred in that scene. Hierarchy path: this TaskInstance --acts_on--> ycb_025_mug --instance_of--> concept:object_drinkware. Its distinct sibling is task_reference_atus_kitchen_food_cleanup_macro at the same ObjectClass. ATUS reports whether this broad primary-activity category was engaged in on a diary day and time spent, not how many discrete actions occurred.

evidence.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey 2024 Table A-1
evidence.scope: Table A-1 reports averages per day for the U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15 years and over, by sex, for 2024. For Food and drink preparation it reports 0.53 average hours per person-day, 60.3 percent average participation per day, and 0.88 average hours among persons who engaged. For Kitchen and food cleanup it reports 0.13 hours per person-day, 22.4 percent participation, and 0.58 hours among persons who engaged. These are annual-average diary-day estimates.
evidence.limitations: The table concerns primary activities: simultaneous secondary activities are excluded. Percent engaged is the share of the population engaging in a category on an average diary day, not a count of events per person or a frequency of any specific primitive action. Published category averages cannot support an object-specific, YCB-specific, robot-task, or execution-time estimate. Values are rounded as published.
evidence.notes: Primary BLS ATUS table A-1. The official tables index identifies this as the table for the civilian noninstitutional population age 15 and over. Table A-1 headers distinguish average hours per day for the population, average percent engaged per day, and average hours for persons who engaged. The table footnote states that a primary activity is the individual's main activity and does not include simultaneous activities. Official index: https://www.bls.gov/tus/tables.htm.

evidence.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2024 ATUS Activity Lexicon with examples
evidence.scope: The Food & Drink Prep., Presentation, & Clean-up grouping has the distinct categories Food and drink preparation, Food presentation, and Kitchen and food clean-up. Preparation examples include cooking, making coffee/tea, mixing drinks, and getting a drink or pouring water into a glass. Cleanup examples include clearing the table, loading/emptying a dishwasher, washing/drying dishes, putting leftovers away, wiping a table, and putting dishes away.
evidence.limitations: The lexicon is a survey coding aid and its examples describe a broad activity code; they are not exhaustive task definitions, robot procedures, or proof that an activity involved any particular object. It provides no population frequency, execution success, asset compatibility, or primitive manipulation duration.
evidence.notes: Primary BLS ATUS 2024 coding lexicon, Food & Drink Prep., Presentation, & Clean-up hierarchy. Used only to justify representing these two source-defined categories as proposed macro-activity crosswalks.

draft_notes: This round creates two distinct sibling macro-activity TaskInstances, not primitive robot tasks: task_reference_atus_food_drink_preparation_macro --acts_on--> ycb_025_mug --instance_of--> concept:object_drinkware, and task_reference_atus_kitchen_food_cleanup_macro --acts_on--> ycb_025_mug --instance_of--> concept:object_drinkware. Each graph walk contains exactly the two existing Atlas hierarchy edges from a TaskInstance through an ObjectInstance to an ObjectClass; the same mug is only a proposed anchor for sibling crosswalks.

ATUS 2024 Table A-1 supplies interpretable category-level annual-average daily participation and duration values for the covered U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 15+: Food and drink preparation (60.3% engaged on an average diary day; 0.53 average hours per person-day; 0.88 average hours among persons who engaged) and Kitchen and food cleanup (22.4%; 0.13; 0.58 respectively). The table reports rounded averages and primary activities, excluding simultaneous secondary activities.

The BLS lexicon's categories encompass heterogeneous activities and examples. The percent-engaged figure is not events per day, the hours are not single-event durations, and neither statistic estimates a primitive robot manipulation or an action involving the selected YCB mug. Any such downscaling would need direct object/action-level observations and an explicitly labeled inference model.

Source links: https://www.bls.gov/tus/tables/a1-2024.pdf ; https://www.bls.gov/tus/lexicons/lexiconwex2024.pdf ; official table index and covered population description: https://www.bls.gov/tus/tables.htm . All Task Atlas task-suitability mappings remain proposed; robot execution, physical assets, and execution times remain unknown or null.
